newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO detains more Arabs for land sale to Jews.
newsitem.headline: PLO detains more Arabs for land sale to Jews.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority, defying criticism over its decision to specify the death penalty for people who sell land to Jews, said on Sunday more than 12 Arabs were in its custody on suspicion of violating the ban.

"More than 12 Palestinians are in custody on suspicion of selling lands. More than six have been detained recently in addition to the six that have already been detained last week," a senior PLO security official told Reuters.
Prosecutor General Khaled al-Kidra confirmed the security official's statement.
Kidra told Reuters that he was studying the case of each detainee very carefully and that any convicted could face the death penalty according to a Jordanian law inherited by the Authority.
"We are still investigating the cases. We still have not brought anyone to trial and we have not prepared charge sheets yet," Kidra said.
He gave no further details about the arrests except that all detainees were West Bank residents.
Last week, the United States strongly criticised Palestinian President Yasser Arafat after an Israeli newspaper quoted him as backing the decision to enforce the death penalty.

The Palestinian Authority, concerned over an Israeli government drive to expand Jewish settlements in the West Bank, recently banned land sales to Jews and its justice minister said a Jordanian law which provides for the death penalty would be applied against offenders.
Jordan controlled the West Bank from 1948 until it lost it to Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
"Land means honour and both are holy, so anyone selling land will be hunted by the law," Kidra said.

Israel has linked the ban on land sales with the recent killings of two Palestinian land dealers found dead in the West Bank. The Authority, which says the law is applied by the courts and not vigilantes, has denied any involvement in the killings.

Palestinians say the purchase of land by Jews and Israeli settlement building in Jerusalem, the rest of the West Bank and Gaza pre-empts final peace talks on the fate of the areas where they hope to establish an independent state.
